meta.title: Playing Modally
meta.summary: Eight questions on what the second chord of a vamp is for, playing across the windows, landing on the characteristic note rather than including it, naming a mode by ear, and writing a vamp of your own.

prompt.text: Which of these are true of the rule that the second chord carries the characteristic note?

spans.text: Ionian gets no vamp at all, because it has no characteristic note for a second chord to carry
Locrian gets no vamp either, because it has no first chord to stand on
Aeolian gets a real loop in
that chord carries is the note Dorian gives up rather than one Aeolian is named for, so the loop cannot pin Aeolian down

explanation.text: The rule has three edges and all three are worth knowing. Ionian's vamp row was already empty when the major family was laid side by side — no characteristic note means no second chord that could assert one. too. The claim that every second chord fits only its own mode is false four times over:
each fit two or three of the seven. And nothing borrows a characteristic note from a neighbour — having none is what makes Ionian and Aeolian the references everything else is measured against.
